episodes.190374: Showers and thunderstorms developed along the dryline across northeast and east central New Mexico around midday Thursday May 30th. A few storms became severe near the Texas state line in Union, Harding, and Quay Counties with one storm producing quarter size hail in Logan. Storms moved east into the Texas Panhandle before sunset. Another round of showers and storms developed along the east slopes of the central mountain chain midday Friday, May 30th becoming severe as they moved east towards the Texas state line. Severe storms in Roosevelt County produced quarter to golf ball size hail, a brief funnel cloud north-northeast of Elida and south-southwest of Dora, and some flash flooding near Floyd. Storms moved east into West Texas shortly after sunset.
episodes.190380: A severe thunderstorm developed in southwest Chaves County along the outflow from storms over the Trans Pecos region in far west Texas during the evening hours. The storm quickly collapsed shortly after 18:00 local time producing a 60 mph wind gust at the Dunken RAWS.
episodes.190440: Severe thunderstorms developed in the mid morning through early afternoon hours and produced several wind gusts and a landspout.
episodes.190442: Severe thunderstorms developed in the mid morning through early afternoon hours and produced several marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.190508: Another day of severe thunderstorms affected the South Plains of West Texas on the evening of the 31st. Broad southeasterly low level atmospheric flow allowed thunderstorms to initially develop in eastern New Mexico. Upscale growth allowed thunderstorms to move into West Texas despite a capped atmosphere over the South Plains. This line of thunderstorms produced widespread severe wind gusts from Hockley County through Lubbock, Lynn, and Garza Counties. The city of Tahoka in Lynn County sustained the most damage due to these strong winds as several structures were damaged. Additionally, pockets of heavy rainfall were observed which caused flash flooding in Lubbock and Lynn Counties.
episodes.190962: A mesoscale convective vortex was situated over the border of southeast Kansas and southwest Missouri during the early afternoon hours on May 31, 2024 before slowly continuing to push northeast over the Missouri Ozarks during the late afternoon/evening and into the overnight hours into June 1, 2024. As this MCV pushed through the Missouri Ozarks, a band of moderate to heavy rain developed along a locally-modified baroclinic boundary, producing a considerable amount of rain over portions of Douglas, Wright, Polk, and Shannon counties. This includes locations that received well over 6 inches of rainfall near Mansfield in Wright County. Additional flooding and heavy rain occurred during the early morning hours on June 1, 2024. Those entries are included in June's portion of Storm Data.
episodes.191008: A wet pattern set up over the Panhandles May 29 through the 31st. Instability in the atmosphere helped to create strong to severe thunderstorms first in the form of discrete cells the night of the 29th into the early AM hours of the 30th. One of which produced a tornado in the western Oklahoma Panhandle. Then subsequent nights disturbances aloft helped create a Mesoscale Convective Complex both on the night of the 30th and again on the 31st. Besides the tornado reported on the 29th this storm in Cimarron County also produced hail up to 1.75��� in diameter. On the next two nights the severe wind gusts reaching upwards of 74 mph. Severe hail was more isolated compared to the winds that were more widespread with lines of storms surging from the northwest to the southeast on the 30th and from the west-northwest to east-southeast on the night of the 31st.
episodes.191107: A slow moving thunderstorm produced up to golf ball size hail and flooding in the town of Sterling. A weaker storm to the east produced hail up to 1 inch in the Haxtun area.
episodes.191134: Widely scattered supercell thunderstorms track across the eastern Colorado plains, mainly along and south of Interstate 70. Large hail, up to 2.25 inches, accompanied the thunderstorms.
episodes.191217: This is a continuation of the heavy rainfall event that started May 31. A mesoscale convective vortex continued to produce heavy rainfall across portions of southern Missouri where localized amounts over 6 inches occurred. This caused flooding of low water crossings and caused rivers to rise into flood stage.
episodes.191327: In the mid-afternoon of the 1st, storms began developing in southeastern Colorado and grew north as the storms moved east. As these storms moved over northwestern Kansas, they produced 0.75 inch hail.
episodes.191375: A thunderstorm developed over the Rapid City area and became severe for a brief time before weakening as it moved onto the Pennington County plains. Hail to half dollar size was reported over parts of Rapid City.
episodes.191381: A thunderstorm briefly became marginally severe on the east side of Rapid City, with hail to quarter size.
episodes.191550: Thunderstorms developed over central Arkansas, training over the same locations, resulting in areas of flash flooding. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches were measured in a short amount of time. Numerous roads between Little Rock to Beebe were impassible.
episodes.191861: Afternoon severe thunderstorms would develop across eastern New Mexico and merge into an MCS that would track through portions of southeast New Mexico and the Permian Basin late in the evening. An outflow boundary from other thunderstorms would also initiate a few supercells ahead of the MCS. Damaging winds, flash flooding, and large hail were all reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.191862: Afternoon severe thunderstorms would develop across eastern New Mexico and merge into an MCS that would track through portions of southeast New Mexico and the Permian Basin late in the evening. An outflow boundary from other thunderstorms would also initiate a few supercells ahead of the MCS. Damaging winds, flash flooding, and large hail were all reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.191893: Elevated river levels along portions of the Little Sioux and Ocheyedan River Basins continued from May into early June due to ongoing wet and rainy conditions.
episodes.192187: Isolated thunderstorms developed shortly after midnight in the central Nebraska Panhandle. This activity moved east into more favorable moisture and shear, becoming severe during the early morning hours of June 1st. Hail up to golf ball size was reported.
episodes.192254: A very dynamic pattern within a longwave trough allowed for a series of major shortwave troughs to propagate over Colorado. This allowed for several days of severe thunderstorms.  Severe thunderstorms were fueled by the conditionally unstable environment with sufficient forcing, high amounts of mid-level moisture, high levels of buoyancy (CAPE), steep lapse rates, and effective bulk shear. This resulted in reports of large hail (in excess of 2 inches), severe wind gusts of greater than 50 kts, and even a few land spouts/funnel clouds.
episodes.192636: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved through Saline, McPherson and Marion counties during the evening hours. It produced nickel to quarter sized hail and 40 to 50 mph winds. Another storm moved through Reno County and produced nickel sized hail.
episodes.192710: Late May heavy rainfall resulted in waters rising on the Green River to moderate flood at Paradise and minor flood at Calhoun. Drier conditions afterwards allowed for a quick decline in river levels early June, with flooding ending June 2nd.
episodes.192722: Torrential rainfall, and training thunderstorms in otherwise widely scattered convection, resulted in an estimated daytime rainfall total of 4 to 7 inches in far southwestern Ballard County and northwestern Carlisle County in Kentucky, along with far eastern Mississippi County in Missouri. This included a mid-morning round of heavy rain, and a second round in the early afternoon. On the Kentucky side of the Mississippi River, flash flooding was reported in Wickliffe and Mayfield Creek overflowed. Precipitable water values were around 1.75 inches, while MLCAPE increased to 1000 J/kg for the afternoon.
episodes.192844: A moist and unstable airmass interacted with upper disturbances that passed across the region during the first and second of the month. Isolated severe weather and flooding resulted from this interaction both afternoons.
episodes.192845: A stalled frontal boundary draped along the Mississippi/Alabama state lines from Tennessee southward was the focus of nocturnal convection. An outflow boundary  developed on the western side of this convection and began to track southwestward. This pulled storms towards the Mississippi sound. One of them interacted with a land breeze boundary near Bay St. Louis which aided in the development of a water spout just offshore.
episodes.192846: Convection initiation on June 1st was fairly typical summertime with storms developing along sea breeze boundaries in the late morning hours. These storms began to grow upscale as daytime heating persisted combined with ample instability and moisture in place. Storms became more widespread and intense as a more organized complex moved into the local forecast area from southwest Louisiana. A handful of storms intensified enough to produce severe hail and damaging winds.
episodes.192919: The dryline pushed just west of the Dell City area allowing for thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon.  An upper trough was moving into the Desert Southwest and helped to trigger isolated storms in far eastern Hudspeth County which produced a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
episodes.192962: A cluster of strong storms produced tree damage in central Mississippi.
episodes.193199: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed on June 1st and advanced east southeastward from North Texas into the Ark-La-Tex during the afternoon and evening hours. These thunderstorms occurred along a sharpening instability gradient, aided by a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV). Modest west to northwesterly mid-level flow provided sufficient effective shear for storm organization, with a threat for supercells within the larger storm cluster. Relatively modest mid-level lapse rates were sufficient for large hail production while damaging wind gusts were the primary threat as strong upscale growth of thunderstorms occurred during peak heating hours. As a result, several damaging wind reports were recorded across Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.193201: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed on June 1st and advanced east southeastward from North Texas into the Ark-La-Tex during the afternoon and evening hours. These thunderstorms occurred along a sharpening instability gradient, aided by a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV). Modest west to northwesterly mid-level flow provided sufficient effective shear for storm organization, with a threat for supercells within the larger storm cluster. Relatively modest mid-level lapse rates were sufficient for large hail production while damaging wind gusts were the primary threat as strong upscale growth of thunderstorms occurred during peak heating hours. As a result, several damaging wind reports were recorded across East Texas along with a few isolated reports of large hail and flash flooding during the afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.193443: A morning funnel cloud was observed.
episodes.193457: Upper level disturbances interacted with leftover surface outflow boundaries from nocturnal MCSs and allowed for scattered strong to severe storms across the region each afternoon from June 1st to June 3rd. A combination of hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding occurred, but an EF-U tornado also occurred in Henderson County on the 3rd. One life was lost June 3rd in Henderson County due to a falling tree in straight-line winds.
episodes.193603: A line of strong thunderstorms produced a very strong wind gust in Haskell County.
episodes.193618: A cluster of strong to severe storms over the Victoria Crossroads moved southeastward into Calhoun County and the Bays of the Middle to Upper Texas Coast. Severe wind gusts were reported in the morning of June 1st, with a later storm survey reporting two capsized boats, RV and shed completely destroyed, loss of shingles, and a snapped power pole near Magnolia Beach in Calhoun County.
episodes.193625: A severe storm over the waters near Matagorda Bay caused strong marine wind gusts and capsized two boats in the morning hours of June 1st.
episodes.193633: Continued troughing across the western CONUS with shortwave impulses moving into the southern Great Plains aided in the development of afternoon severe thunderstorms and localized flash flooding across the Davis Mountains and vicinity.
episodes.193669: A high based shower collapsed and produced a 60 mph wind gust at the Lander airport.
episodes.193687: A moist and unstable airmass interacted with upper disturbances that passed across the region during the first and second of June. Scattered severe weather and flooding resulted from this interaction both afternoons.
episodes.193715: Gusty outflow wind gusts were measured in southwest Wyoming.
episodes.193836: Mostly zonal flow aloft advected some modest midlevel moisture into northern portions of eastern Utah and western Colorado in the days leading up to this event. This moisture, combined with some low-end instability, set the stage form some isolated showers and thunderstorms to form over the higher terrain. A passing weak shortwave trough added some extra lift and energy to the region on the 1st, resulting in some stronger showers and thunderstorms capable of producing strong, gusty winds. In addition, dry surface levels led to precipitation from these storms evaporating before reaching the surface, thus also enhancing winds.
